subject: Capacity true-up & staged uplift options for Q4
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Kapoor <claire.kapoor@somahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Capacity true-up & staged uplift options for Q4

Hi Claire,

Thanks again for the time on Friday. Based on your note about a mid-quarter spike in inference usage, I pulled together a couple of pragmatic paths we can take to cover the additional capacity while keeping cost predictable for the rest of the year. High level: one-time true-up + pro-rated add-on OR staged uplift with a small discount if you commit to an extended co-term.

Options (summary):
- Option A — True-up only: bill usage through Oct as a one-time true-up invoice; no change to term.
- Option B — Staged uplift (recommended): add a Q4 uplift bucket + 6-month co-term extension; 7.5% credit applied to uplift if confirmed by 11/10.
- Option C — Annualize now: convert uplift to a 12-month annualized commit for a deeper discount (12%) and priority capacity.

I attached a short workbook with example numbers and the SOW amendment draft. Can we set a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk options with your engineering and procurement leads?

Next steps I suggest:
1) Review workbook (attached)
2) Quick sync (30m) to pick a path and confirm procurement timeline
3) Redwood sends SOW amendment + pricing appendix

Attachment: Soma_Uplift_Workbook_v3.xlsx (1 spreadsheet, 48 KB)
Attachment: SOW_Amendment_Draft.docx (word draft, 22 KB)

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0182

Ben,

Thanks — that framing is helpful. A couple of quick questions from our side before we jump on a call:
- Does the pro-rated uplift (Option B) require changing the current invoice frequency or will it appear as a one-off invoice?
- For Option C, can you confirm how the 12% discount is applied (on committed tokens only, or across usage)?
- We also need procurement to see the SOW language for data residency and audit rights.

Procurement: can you share the earliest approval window? We are trying to avoid interrupting any clinical workloads.

Happy to take a 30m tomorrow afternoon if that works for you — cc'd our procurement lead to coordinate.

Best,

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-02T09:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity true-up & staged uplift options for Q4

Claire — thanks, quick answers inline and a proposal below.

- Invoice mechanics (Option B): The staged uplift appears as a one-time invoice for the uplift bucket, then the existing cadence continues. We can also convert it into a recurring monthly add-on if procurement prefers.
- Discount scope (Option C): 12% applies to committed capacity (tokens/units) for the annualized portion; overages billed at standard usage rates. I'll call this out explicitly in the SOW appendix.
- SOW language: the draft in the workbook has the data residency and audit paragraph; procurement should flag edits and we'll incorporate.

My recommended path (practical tradeoff):
1) Take Option B (staged uplift) to immediately cover Q4 capacity and avoid clinical risk.
2) If Soma can commit to a 6–12 month co-term by 11/10, Redwood will apply a 7.5% uplift credit up front.
3) If Soma converts to a 12-month annualized commit within 30 days, we will apply an additional 4.5% credit (total 12% on the annualized portion).

Example numbers (illustrative):
- Current commit: 100k token units/month
- Q4 uplift need: +40k token units/month (Nov-Dec)
- Option B cost (after 7.5% uplift credit): ~$27,600 one-time uplift invoice (pro-rated)

I attached a new tab in the workbook that shows the invoice view and a SOW amendment redline.

Proposed call windows: 11/02 2:00–2:30pm PT or 11/03 10:00–10:30am PT. Which works?

(Attachment: Soma_Uplift_Workbook_v3.xlsx — updated tab)

Thanks,
Ben
